claim: deploy.yml (Deploy to Production) acts only on this repository's own pushes to main, as far as a strict text reader can hold it. ci-gate carries no job-level if (plain, quoted or spaced key) and one refusal step equal, line for line, to the allowed text: it reads the triggering run's event and head repository through env and exits 1 unless they are 'push' and this repository; ci-gate writes neither GITHUB_ENV nor GITHUB_OUTPUT. The on: block equals the allowed one and no defaults: is set. The jobs: block holds only plain job keys (a quoted, flow-style, anchored or aliased job key, a quoted or spaced key inside a job, a tab or a duplicate fails), the job set is fixed, and each job's single job-level if (block scalars read with their blank lines) equals the one allowed: every workflow_run-startable job requires the own-push group, rollback-guide is dispatch-only; no job is a reusable-workflow call; nothing sets continue-on-error. Held by scripts/check_deploy_own_pushes.py (gate-owned, run with python3 -I), whose --self-test plants 33 breaks, every evasion the round-2 ADR 0090 audit found among them; run by scripts/test_pr_audit_gate.py. Not held: ci-gate's first step (the conclusion check, pinned separately by ADR-0097's row) and GitHub's own YAML evaluation (a form this reader accepts but GitHub reads differently) (workflow_run runs main's copy, so the step first runs on the merge commit's Deploy run). Consequence disclosed to the founder: a CI run started by workflow_dispatch on main (pr_audit_gate.py's CI-side merge re-entry) is refused too. Founder, 2026-09-30, on #534, verbatim pick: "Sign off, add deploy fix (Recommended)".
